categoryName: Packaged & instant food — noodles, pasta, ready-to-eat, soups, sauces, jams, spreads, pickles, papad

skuLines.examples: Maggi 2-Minute Masala 70g; Sunfeast Yippee Magic Masala 60g; Top Ramen Masala; Patanjali Atta Noodles
skuLines.packSizes: 60-80 g single; 140 g / 280 g 2-in-1 and 4-in-1 pouches
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; collapses during school vacation weeks, peaks in exam fortnights and in June before monsoon road closures
skuLines.marginBand: 4-10% (MRP-locked national brand; distributor scheme income adds 1-3%)
skuLines.notes: The single highest-velocity SKU in a hostel township — a stockout here sends a whole hostel wing's wallet off-campus. ~9-month shelf life; buy full cases (96/144-pc) so hill freight per unit stays sane.

skuLines.examples: Maggi 8-pack 560g; Maggi 12-pack carton; Yippee 6-in-1; Top Ramen 4-pack
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes at session start and pre-monsoon stock-up
skuLines.notes: Multi-serve is the fastest-growing pack cut in India (~13.4% CAGR) largely because it saves freight and handling per unit — exactly the economics of 40 km of hill road.

skuLines.examples: Maggi Chatpata; Yippee Saucy Masala; Ching's Hot Garlic / Chilli Chow; Wai Wai Xpress
skuLines.notes: Masala is still ~80% of the Indian noodle market — keep flavour depth to 3-4 SKUs or the tail turns into dead stock behind the masala wall.

skuLines.line: Instant noodles — atta / millet / oats / low-sodium
skuLines.examples: Maggi Atta Noodles; ITC YiPPee millet noodles; Slurrp Farm millet noodles; Saffola Oodles
skuLines.notes: The defensible premium of 2026 (millet + air-dried + clean label). The buyer is a married staff parent with a small child, not a hostel student — merchandise it near baby/health, not next to the ₹14 Maggi.

skuLines.examples: Maggi Cuppa Mania; Nissin Cup Noodles; Yippee Cup; Wai Wai Quick cup
skuLines.seasonality: Spikes Oct-Mar (cold), on exam nights, and every evening the mess closes early
skuLines.notes: Right format where a hostel room has a kettle and no stove — cups are growing ~14.3% CAGR vs packets. Bulky: they cube out the truck, so order them with light freight, never with cans.

skuLines.examples: Nongshim Shin Ramyun / Veggie Ramyun; Indo Nissin Geki; Koka; MAMA; Samyang Buldak only where FSSAI veg-marked
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round, K-pop/K-drama driven; peaks at term start when pocket money is fresh
skuLines.marginBand: 20-35% — the best margin in this whole lane
skuLines.notes: Two hard gates: (1) pure-veg campus — most Buldak 'hot chicken' SKUs are NOT vegetarian, buy only green-dot/veg-marked variants; (2) grey imports without an FSSAI importer sticker are a licence risk. Fastest-growing noodle segment in India (~13.3% CAGR).

skuLines.line: Asian dry noodles — hakka, chowmein, rice sticks
skuLines.examples: Ching's Secret Veg Hakka Noodles 140g/280g; Ching's rice noodles; Tai Pan; Koka rice sticks
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks around campus functions and family cooking for guests
skuLines.notes: Never sells alone — planogram with soy sauce, chilli sauce and schezwan chutney as a set. Light, 9-12 month life, ideal hill stock.

skuLines.examples: Maggi Pazzta Cheese Macaroni; Maggi Pazzta Masala Penne; Sunfeast Pasta Treat; Knorr instant pasta
skuLines.notes: Cheese variants are what move with 10-16 year olds. Cup form needs only a kettle, so it works in a hostel room where cooking is banned.

skuLines.examples: Bambino penne / fusilli / elbow macaroni 400-500g; Sunfeast pasta; Weikfield macaroni
skuLines.notes: 18-24 month shelf life, unbreakable, cheap per kg of freight — one of the safest lines to deep-stock as monsoon road-closure buffer.

skuLines.examples: Del Monte penne; Borges spaghetti; Barilla; Chef's Basket
skuLines.notes: Thin buyer pool (faculty, international-curriculum families). Cap at 4-6 facings or it ages on shelf at ₹300 a pack.

skuLines.examples: Bambino atta pasta; Yoga Bar protein pasta; quinoa pasta; multigrain fusilli
skuLines.notes: Rides the 2026 protein wave (86% of Indian snack buyers weigh protein, ~32% pay a premium). Start with 2 SKUs and let offtake decide.

skuLines.examples: Bambino roasted vermicelli 400g/850g; MTR vermicelli; Nilon's seviyan
skuLines.seasonality: Spikes hard at Gurpurab, Baisakhi, Lohri, Diwali and any langar (kheer/upma) — indent 2-3x normal before festival weeks
skuLines.notes: Roasted outsells plain in the North. Crumbles if cartons are bottom-loaded in a hill truck — top-load only.

skuLines.examples: Bambino 1 kg; Weikfield 1 kg; institutional 5 kg elbow macaroni
skuLines.notes: Belongs in the warehouse line, not on the POS shelf. Two canteens plus the mess make this a predictable indent — best on a quarterly rate contract.

skuLines.examples: Veeba pasta sauce; Del Monte pizza & pasta sauce; Dr Oetker FunFoods; Ching's
skuLines.notes: Glass jars are the classic hill-road casualty — prefer PET/pouch and carry a 1-2% breakage allowance. Needs refrigeration after opening; say so at the counter or you get returns.

skuLines.examples: MTR Paneer Butter Masala 300g (~₹149); Haldiram's Minute Khana Dal Makhani ₹100 / Rajma ₹85 / Chole; Gits Dal Makhani ₹106; ITC Kitchens of India
skuLines.seasonality: Spikes in monsoon (Jul-Sep) road closures, in winter, and whenever the mess is shut
skuLines.notes: 12-18 month ambient life, zero cold chain — the best-fitting product in the entire store for a township that can be cut off for days. Pure-veg SKUs only; read every label, several brands run non-veg variants in identical artwork.

skuLines.examples: MTR veg biryani / pulao; Gits khichdi; Tasty Bite rice meals; Kitchens of India dal-chawal
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon and winter; also when staff travel down to town
skuLines.notes: Slower than the curries because rice is trivially easy to cook. Keep shallow and watch dates — hill deliveries often land with 30-40% of shelf life already burnt.

skuLines.line: Instant breakfast mixes — idli, dosa, upma, poha
skuLines.examples: MTR Rice Idli mix ₹101; MTR Rava Idli 500g; Gits Dosa mix ₹126; Gits Upma 200g ₹60; MTR 3-Minute Poha 60g ₹27
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; South-Indian staff households and Navratri/fasting weeks lift it
skuLines.notes: Flour-based, so it cakes and attracts weevils in a Sirmaur monsoon. Dry, raised, sealed storage and only 3-4 weeks' cover Jul-Sep.

skuLines.line: Instant snack mixes — dhokla, vada, pakoda
skuLines.examples: Gits Dhokla; Gits Khaman; Gits Idli-Vada; MTR Bajji / Bonda mix
skuLines.seasonality: Festival weeks, parents' visiting days, guest season
skuLines.notes: Same humidity caveat as breakfast mixes — do not deep-stock into the monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Gits Gulab Jamun mix; Gits Jalebi; MTR kheer / halwa mix; Weikfield & Brown & Polson custard powder; Weikfield jelly
skuLines.seasonality: Big spikes at Gurpurab, Baisakhi, Lohri, Diwali, birthdays and langar; jelly and custard spike in summer
skuLines.notes: Gulab jamun mix is the festival hero on a Sikh campus — indent in langar quantities, not retail quantities, and place the order 3 weeks before the gurpurab.

skuLines.examples: Saffola Classic Masala Oats 38g ₹20 / 225g ₹100 / Cuppa 52g ₹53; Quaker Masala Magic; Kellogg's oats
skuLines.packSizes: 38 g sachet; 52-70 g cup; 225-750 g pack
skuLines.notes: Kettle-only. This is the 'I want something other than noodles' SKU that keeps a hostel wallet on campus instead of on a trip to town.

skuLines.line: Instant porridge / dalia / ragi malt / sattu
skuLines.examples: Manna ragi malt; Patanjali dalia; Bagrry's porridge; instant sattu mix
skuLines.notes: Overlaps the baby-food lane — coordinate so the same ragi SKU isn't bought twice into two departments. Real demand from married staff with toddlers and from older residents.

skuLines.examples: Nutrela soya chunks 200g/1kg; Sohum soya; Fortune soya chunks
skuLines.notes: In a strictly vegetarian, no-egg township this is the protein workhorse — merchandise it with instant food rather than burying it in staples. Feather-light freight, 9-12 month life.

skuLines.examples: Knorr Classic Sweet Corn / Hot & Sour / Tomato / Creamy Mushroom; Maggi Sanjeevani soup; Ching's soup
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp Oct-Mar spike — a cold hill campus makes soup a seasonal hero; plan 3-4x summer volumes for Nov-Jan
skuLines.notes: Powder cakes in monsoon damp: buy shallow Jul-Sep, then build the winter pile from late September so you are not chasing stock in December snow.

skuLines.examples: Knorr Cup-a-Soup Mixed Vegetable 10-11g (~₹9-12); Knorr Tomato Cup-a-Soup; Maggi single-serve soup
skuLines.notes: The ₹10 impulse SKU that makes the Ary Lite counter work on a cold evening. Put a hot-water flask next to it and it sells itself.

skuLines.examples: Knorr Professional soup 500g/1kg; institutional tomato / sweet corn packs
skuLines.notes: Warehouse line on a rate contract. One 1 kg pack replaces ~20 retail sachets of packaging and freight up the hill.

skuLines.examples: Kissan Fresh Tomato Ketchup 850g (~₹93); Maggi Rich Tomato 850g-1kg; Nilon's; Tops
skuLines.packSizes: 500 g, 850 g, 1 kg pouch or bottle
skuLines.notes: Doypack over glass for hill freight. This is the anchor of the condiment bay — never let it go empty, everything around it sells off its footfall.

skuLines.examples: Kissan 200g squeezy; Maggi 100-200g; 8-10 g sachets in 100-pc jars
skuLines.notes: Sachets are how canteens and tiffin-carrying children actually buy ketchup. Stock the sachet jar as its own line with its own reorder point.

skuLines.examples: Kissan 2 kg doypack; Del Monte 1 kg; Foodrite 5 kg tomato sauce
skuLines.notes: Institutional grade, separate from the retail SKU — keep the indent and the shelf apart or the canteen price cannibalises the POS shelf.

skuLines.line: Chinese sauce set — soy, chilli, vinegar
skuLines.examples: Ching's Secret soy / green chilli / red chilli sauce; Weikfield synthetic vinegar; Sil; Wingreens
skuLines.notes: Sell as a three-bottle set alongside hakka noodles. PET only — glass vinegar bottles break more often than anything else in this lane.

skuLines.examples: Ching's Schezwan Chutney 250g; Smith & Jones schezwan; Veeba schezwan
skuLines.notes: One of the highest-pull SKUs with 15-25 year olds — it turns plain mess rice into a meal they actually want. Refrigerate after opening.

skuLines.examples: Veeba Veg Eggless Mayonnaise 250g / 875g; Dr Oetker FunFoods Veg Mayo; Wingreens eggless mayo
skuLines.notes: EGGLESS ONLY — the campus is pure vegetarian, and eggless is the mainstream Indian format anyway. 6-9 month life, refrigerate after opening; keep stock off any sun-facing wall in May-June.

skuLines.examples: Veeba tandoori / peri-peri mayo; Wingreens mint & jalapeño dips; Dr Oetker thousand island; salsa; hummus
skuLines.notes: Fastest-innovating condiment space in India (mayo market ~7.6% CAGR, driven by QSR-style eating at home). Start with tandoori and peri-peri only, then widen.

skuLines.examples: Tabasco; Veeba sriracha; Nando's peri-peri; Kissan chilli garlic; barbecue sauce
skuLines.notes: High-margin long tail but genuinely slow. 4-6 SKUs, single facings, and diary the 18-month expiry — this is where dead stock hides.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Hommade tomato puree 200g/1kg; Kissan puree; Ching's Manchurian / Hakka cooking kit
skuLines.seasonality: Spikes when hill tomato prices spike (Dec-Feb) and after monsoon crop damage
skuLines.notes: A real substitute good in a cut-off location — the week the vegetable truck does not come up the hill, puree clears out. Worth a standing buffer.

skuLines.examples: Mother's Recipe mint / tamarind chutney; Tops garlic chutney; Neo; Dabur imli chutney
skuLines.notes: Pairs directly with the ready-to-fry gol gappa / papdi line — merchandise the two together and both lift.

skuLines.examples: Kissan Mixed Fruit Jam 200g / 500g / 700g; Tops mixed fruit; Mala's; Patanjali
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks through the school session, dips in vacations
skuLines.notes: Bread-and-jam is the default hostel breakfast add-on and a top-5 line for children. 18-24 month life; prefer PET, the 700 g glass jars break in transit.

skuLines.line: Jam — single fruit, premium, marmalade, no-added-sugar
skuLines.examples: Kissan strawberry / pineapple; Mala's apple & apricot; Bonne Maman; St Dalfour no-added-sugar; local Himachali apple jam
skuLines.seasonality: Visitor and gifting season; local apple/apricot preserve sells to visiting parents as a Himachal souvenir
skuLines.marginBand: 20-35% — local HP-made is the best margin, with almost no freight
skuLines.notes: Sourcing apple, apricot and plum preserve from within Himachal removes freight, adds a story, and gives ARY a line nobody else sells to this campus.

skuLines.examples: Nutella 290-350g; Hershey's spread; Cadbury Choco Delight; Dr Oetker FunFoods choco
skuLines.seasonality: Session-time; birthday and gifting spikes; separates in a hot store room in May-June
skuLines.notes: Enormous pull with 8-18 year olds and a classic wallet-leaks-to-town item when missing. Store below 25°C — easy in Baru Sahib except in the summer store room.

skuLines.examples: Pintola All Natural / High Protein 350g-1kg; Sundrop crunchy; Alpino; MyFitness chocolate peanut butter
skuLines.notes: The protein-trend winner and a genuinely useful protein source on a no-egg campus — India's spreads market is compounding ~17%. Oil separation is normal; tell buyers to stir or you will field complaints.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Honey 250g / 500g / 1kg; Patanjali honey; Zandu; local Sirmaur forest honey
skuLines.notes: Crystallises in a cold hill store — normal, but train the counter to explain it. Local raw honey is a zero-freight, high-margin line worth sourcing in-district.

skuLines.examples: FunFoods veg sandwich spread; Veeba sandwich spread; almond butter; tahini
skuLines.notes: Keep to 2-3 SKUs. Refrigerate after opening; short 6-9 month life on the mayo-based spreads.

skuLines.examples: Mother's Recipe mango pickle 400g / 1kg; Priya avakaya; Nilon's mango; Pachranga
skuLines.packSizes: 200 g, 400 g, 500 g, 1 kg jar; 500 g pouch
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; retail dips May-June when families make their own in the mango season
skuLines.notes: Glass-jar breakage is the main hidden loss on this line — buy pouch where available, freight jars upright and strawed. 12-24 month life; oil settling on top is normal, not spoilage.

skuLines.examples: Mother's Recipe mixed & lemon pickle; Tops garlic pickle; Nilon's chilli; Bedekar
skuLines.notes: Lemon and mixed are the North Indian volume flavours after mango. Four to six flavour SKUs is the whole assortment; more is dead money in glass.

skuLines.examples: Pachranga mixed pickle; gobhi-gajar-shalgam achar; Amritsari-style mixed; local galgal (hill lemon) and lingdi pickle
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Feb only — a true winter SKU for a Punjabi/Himachali population; place the whole year's order in October
skuLines.notes: Galgal and lingdi pickle are Sirmaur specialities: no freight, high margin, and a line no outside store is selling to these 5,000 residents. Source from local women's groups.

skuLines.examples: Mother's Recipe 15 g sachets; institutional 10-15 g pickle sachets in 100-pc boxes
skuLines.notes: How a canteen thali and a school tiffin actually get pickle. Buy by the box and sell both retail at the counter and wholesale to the two canteens.

skuLines.examples: 5 kg mango / mixed pickle tin or jar; local SHG bulk supply
skuLines.notes: The mess is the volume buyer. A local women's-group supplier will beat any branded landed cost once 40 km of hill freight is added to the branded tin.

skuLines.examples: Dabur amla murabba; apple and harad murabba; amla candy; gur-based preserves
skuLines.notes: Ayurvedic-leaning demand from older residents; overlaps the health/ayurveda lane, so agree who buys it.

skuLines.examples: Lijjat Udad Papad 200g (~₹77-95); Lijjat moong papad; Bikaji; local Punjabi/HP papad
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round, with large spikes at langar, festivals and guest weeks
skuLines.notes: Absorbs monsoon damp and goes leathery — airtight storage, shallow stock Jul-Sep, strict FIFO. Also the most transit-fragile item in the lane: breakage, not expiry, is what kills the margin.

skuLines.examples: Lijjat Punjabi Masala 200g; Lijjat jeera / red chilli; Bikaji Baatcheet 400g; roasted no-fry papad snack packs
skuLines.packSizes: 200 g, 400 g; 25-50 g roasted snack packs
skuLines.notes: Ready-roasted small packs are a counter snack needing no frying — a good fit for hostel rooms where frying is not allowed.

skuLines.examples: Sabudana papad; rice khichiya; Gujarati khichiya; local jeera khichiya
skuLines.seasonality: Navratri and fasting weeks (Chaitra and Sharad), plus the summer sun-drying season
skuLines.notes: A fasting-season line. Needs frying, so it is a family purchase, never a hostel one.

skuLines.examples: Unfried gol gappa / puri; papdi; fryums (chakri, ring, alphabet); mathri; sev
skuLines.seasonality: Chaat season, campus functions, parents' visiting days
skuLines.marginBand: 25-40% — mostly local/unbranded, the best margin in the lane
skuLines.notes: Bulky and crush-prone: buy from the nearest Punjab/HP supplier rather than a national brand, and never bottom-load. Merchandise beside the chutney line.

skuLines.examples: American Garden baked beans; Del Monte sweet corn and pineapple slices; Weikfield mushrooms; Figaro olives; tinned tomatoes
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; baked beans and sweet corn lift in winter
skuLines.notes: Worst freight economics in the lane (heavy per rupee of sale), so hold 8-12 fast SKUs only — but the 24-month life makes it a legitimate monsoon buffer. Reject dented or rusted cans on receipt.

skuLines.examples: McCain french fries / aloo tikki / smiles; Sumeru or ID veg momos; frozen paratha; frozen green peas
skuLines.notes: Only viable with a working deep freezer AND power backup — one monsoon outage writes off the whole stock. Reefer freight up 40 km of hill road is the real gate; the sane version of this line is canteen supply only, not retail.

trends2026: Cup and bowl formats are the growth engine: packets still hold ~74.6% share but cups/bowls are compounding ~14.3% a year, driven by hostels, offices and transit — exactly the format a kettle-only hostel room needs.

Korean/K-flavour is the fastest-growing noodle segment in India (~13.3% CAGR); Korean-style searches are up over 200% since 2022 and mainstream players now launch Korean-heat × Indian-masala hybrids at ₹55-60 (Indo Nissin Geki, Nestlé BBQ Korean), creating a real premium tier above Maggi.
Millet, atta, air-dried and low-sodium reformulation is the defensible premium (ITC YiPPee millet, Slurrp Farm), sold on clean-label FSSAI claims to parents rather than to students.

Protein has moved from the health shelf into everyday packaged food — 86% of Indian snack buyers now weigh protein and ~32% will pay a premium — so peanut butter, protein pasta and high-protein oats become core lines, not curiosities.

Ready-to-eat and ready-to-cook are the fastest-growing packaged-food block (RTE ~16% CAGR to USD 3.18 bn by 2031; RTC forecast ~25% CAGR), with hyperlocal regional flavours being launched and the ₹85-165 ambient 300 g retort pouch becoming a normal weekday dinner.

Eggless flavoured mayonnaise and Indianised dips (tandoori, peri-peri, schezwan) are the most active innovation space in condiments (mayo ~7.6% CAGR) — and eggless is precisely what a pure-vegetarian campus requires.
Sweet spreads and nut butters are compounding ~14-17% a year, with low-sugar, no-added-sugar and clean-label variants widening the shelf well beyond mixed-fruit jam.

Quick commerce (~₹11,000 Cr GMV in a single month, roughly doubling year on year) is resetting expectations even where it cannot deliver: platforms are pivoting to gourmet and premium for margin while the ₹5-30 pack remains the volume driver — the winning shape is a barbell (cheap sachet plus genuine premium), not a thick middle.
adjacentServices: Hot-water / kettle counter at Ary Lite — sell the cup noodle, cup soup or masala oats made and served rather than as a packet; a ₹15 sachet becomes a ₹35-40 served item, the highest-margin service attachable to this lane.

Institutional supply line to the two canteens and the mess — bulk ketchup, eggless mayo, pickle, macaroni and soup mix on a quarterly rate contract, indented from the warehouse rather than sold off the POS shelf.
Hostel starter kit as a single boxed SKU at admission and session start — noodles, cup soup, jam, ketchup sachets, papad, pickle sachets.
Parent-funded monthly snack top-up: parents pay online from anywhere, ARY packs and delivers to the hostel warden — recurring revenue at a much higher average bill than the ₹208 walk-in.
Pre-monsoon buffer bundle for staff families, sold in June: a two-week shelf-stable food box (retort curries, noodles, pasta, puree, soup) bought before the Sirmaur roads start closing.
Festival and langar indent desk — papad, vermicelli, gulab jamun mix and pickle in langar quantities for Gurpurab, Baisakhi, Lohri and Diwali, ordered three weeks ahead.

Local consignment shelf: Sirmaur and Punjabi pickle, papad, galgal and lingdi achar, and Himachali apple/apricot jam from local women's groups — 25-40% margin, zero freight, and a souvenir line for visiting parents.
Near-expiry markdown rack with a printed expiry policy, because hill deliveries routinely arrive with a third of shelf life already gone — turning an inevitable write-off into a discount sale.
